jobs.title: Principal Data Product Manager
jobs.description:
This role welcomes full remote or hybrid work arrangements. However, applicants must be based in Spain, Italy or France and have a work permit to be considered .

ABOUT LAUNCHMETRICS
Launchmetrics is the leading Brand Performance Cloud used by Fashion, Lifestyle and Beauty (FLB) executives to make smarter decisions around their branding efforts.
With over a decade of industry expertise, we have helped more than 1,200 customers create inspiring, impactful and measurable experiences.
Founded in NYC and with operating headquarters in Paris, we have employees in ten markets worldwide and offer support in five languages. We have been the trusted brand performance technology to brands worldwide such as Dior, Fendi, Shiseido, NET-A-PORTER and Adidas as well as industry partners like IMG, the Council of Fashion Designers of America, the British Fashion Council, and Camera Nazionale Della Moda Italiana.
How we work: pods and crafts
We recently moved our Product and Tech teams to a pod model, and it changes the shape of this job in ways worth understanding before you apply.

• A pod is a small group, 1 to 4 people, that owns a single mission end to end: from scoping and building through cleaning, enablement and watching adoption. Pods form around a mission and dissolve when it's done. Everyone is a pod owner, from the most junior person to the most senior, because ownership is the point.

• Your craft is your main area of expertise: Design, Tech, or Data. It's the discipline you go deep in.

• Your domain is your product-area home, the part of our software suite you know best. Pods change with every mission; your craft and your domain don't.

ABOUT THE ROLE
We're looking for a Principal Data Product Manager with a Data expertise to own missions on our Data Collection and Enrichment Systems.
At Launchmetrics, the core of our Metrics value comes from the data we deliver through our SaaS solution. Our client buy data as much as they buy access to a platform.
The Data Collection and Enrichment domain is in charge of collecting the data, enriching it and making it accessible in an efficient and reliable manner to the other domains. If you like the idea of owning a problem end to end, care about data quality the way other people care about pixel alignment, and want to work on forward thinking and AI centric projects, this role is for you.
As a Principal Data Product Manager here, you'll own missions on that domain from scoping to adoption, and you'll be one of the references for building our Data strategy, with the support of our VP Product. You operate as a fully autonomous pod owner.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Talk to your users. A lot. Turn the needs of customers and internal teams into product requirements that can be measured, and work with engineers day to day to deliver them.

• Own missions end to end. Scope, build with the pod, enable and monitor adoption for Data Platform missions, keeping a clear source of truth so everyone can see where things stand.

• Master our data flow. Work across acquisition, enrichment (manual, rule-based and AI-based) and management (datalake, APIs) to make data delivery faster and more reliable.

• Measure what matters. Define the metrics and KPIs for adoption and performance of what you build, then actually analyse them and feed the learnings back into prioritisation.

• Keep an eye on the market. Stay close to the competitive landscape and where brand measurement is heading, and let that sharpen your thinking.

• Collaborate with stakeholders. Collaborate with engineers, business stakeholders and leadership, speaking the right language to each.

• Raise the bar around you. Contribute to shared tooling and processes, and help the data domain get sharper over time.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
This role sits at the Principal stage of our framework. Concretely, that means:

• Experience. Around 5 and 10 years in product management or data management, ideally shipping alongside engineers in a SaaS environment.

• Deep in Data. You're fluent in SQL and comfortable with data modelling, pipelines and APIs. You understand the data lifecycle, from acquisition to delivery, and you can assess and improve the quality of what flows through it. A few years working on data, analytics or data-product problems alongside engineers.

• Business sense. You understand our industry and our customers well enough to know why one kind of data matters to them and another doesn't, and you're curious about the branding challenges fashion and luxury brands face.

• A real discovery instinct. You start from the problem, not the solution, and you're happy talking to users and turning fuzzy needs into something measurable.

• Self-sufficient across crafts. You're not a designer or a PM, but you can do enough product thinking and rough interface reasoning to keep a small pod moving without waiting for someone else.

• Clear and trusted. You communicate simply with both technical and business people, follow through on what you own, and people come to rely on you as the reference for your scope.

• Clear communication and fluent English. You can explain your thinking, you're comfortable in a fast-paced environment, and you're keen to learn. Our team is international; other languages are a welcome bonus.

WHERE THIS ROLE CAN GROW
In the Product team, people grow by going deeper in their craft and by expanding their scope across five stages (Junior, Mid, Senior, Principal, Lead), and by taking on modular add-on responsibilities (Ops, Client Representativity, Strategy, Management).
As a Principal Product Manager, you can already pick up the Ops add-on (owning a shared tool, or a Claude skill) and some Strategy responsibilities. We're looking for someone who can grow into leading our Data strategy, so there are a few more stages ahead. As it progresses, expect a deeper focus on Strategy, along with new areas like Management and Client Representativity.

RECRUITMENT PROCESS

• Intro call with Talent Acquisition, to get to know each other (30 min).

• Meet & Greet with Hiring Manager on the team, the domain and the pod model.

• Brainstorming session with our PMs

• Data and Product case you prepare, then present to a couple of PMs: a real data problem, scoped and reasoned through.

• Team fit with the engineers and peers you'd build alongside.

WHY YOU’LL LOVE LAUNCHMETRICS
We're a company that prioritizes people, fostering a relaxed yet dynamic atmosphere. Our international team is filled with enthusiastic, motivated individuals who enjoy their work. Autonomy empowers our team members, allowing them to make a substantial difference in our business, for our customers, and within our organization. When you become part of our team, you'll have access to growth and advancement possibilities, including a learning and development allowance, a benefits package tailored to each location, and flexible work arrangements, along with support for establishing your home office and other perks.

OUR COMMITMEN

jobs.title: Principal Product Manager, Billing & Marketplaces
jobs.description:
ClickHouse Cloud, the fully managed version of the open source ClickHouse database, is available on AWS, GCP, and Azure. Customers can purchase directly from ClickHouse or through the cloud marketplaces. Billing is how every ClickHouse product reaches customers and shows up in our financials. As we add new products and new ways to buy, we are investing in our billing platform to scale with them. As Principal Product Manager for Billing and Marketplaces, you will lead that work and report to the Director of Product Management, Billing and Marketplaces.

What You Will Do

• Own the multi-year vision, strategy, and roadmap for billing, from usage metering through invoicing, payments, and revenue recognition, working alongside the product managers and engineering leads of our metering and pricing, billing platform, and payments teams.

• Evolve our metering and pricing foundation into a single metrics pipeline that new products can reuse, where the same metric can be priced differently by product and tier, and only net-new metrics need code changes.

• Evolve our prepaid commit capabilities, with flexibility for customer-specific rate cards or metric-level discounts, contract changes and rollovers, and customer-facing balance visibility and spend alerts.

• Own our cloud marketplace strategy and integrations across AWS, GCP, and Azure, including private offers, usage reporting, and subscription linking.

• Lead the evaluation of billing architecture, from build versus buy decisions and POCs through migration plans and a clear recommendation to senior leadership.

• Give Finance, Data, and Sales Ops systems they can trust, including ERP and revenue recognition sync, period close, audit controls, and SOX and SOC 2 readiness.

• Partner with product teams, Product Marketing, Sales, and Support to launch billing for new products and pricing models, and serve as the company's subject matter expert on how customers are billed.

• Mentor other product managers and help build the team.

About You

• 10+ years of product management experience, including 5+ years owning billing, metering, payments, or commercial platforms for a cloud or usage-based product.

• Deep expertise in usage-based pricing, prepaid credits, and committed spend contracts, and in how they translate into systems, invoices, and revenue.

• Hands-on experience with AWS, GCP, or Azure marketplaces, including private offers, co-sell, entitlements, metering APIs, and disbursements.

• Familiarity with payments across card, invoice, marketplace, and partner channels, including dunning and delinquency flows, fraud detection, and payment notifications.

• Strong understanding of order-to-cash, including invoicing, payment processing, tax, multi-currency, ERP integration, and revenue recognition.

• Experience with third-party billing and payment platforms, such as Stripe or a usage-based billing vendor.

• A track record of designing and maturing a product area from v1 and leading complex programs across engineering, Finance, and go-to-market teams.

• Excellent written and verbal communication, including presenting trade-offs to executives and explaining billing concepts to non-technical audiences.

Bonus Points

• Experience at an infrastructure, database, or developer platform company.

• Comfortable going deep with engineers on event-driven architectures, data pipelines, and idempotency, and fluent enough in SQL to analyze billing data yourself.

• Speaking or published thought leadership on usage-based pricing, billing, or cloud marketplaces.

Perks

• Flexible work environment - ClickHouse is a globally distributed company and remote-friendly. We currently operate in over 25 countries.

• Healthcare - Employer contributions towards your healthcare.

• Equity in the company - Every new eligible team member who joins our company receives equity.

• Time off - Flexible time off in the US, generous entitlement in other countries.

• A USD$500 Home office setup if you’re a remote employee.

• Global Gatherings – We believe in the power of in-person connection and offer opportunities to engage with colleagues at company-wide offsites.

Culture - We All Shape It

As part of a rapidly scaling start-up, you will be instrumental in shaping our culture.

Are you interested in finding out more about our culture? Learn more about our values here. Check out our blog posts or follow us on LinkedIn to find out more about what’s happening at ClickHouse.

Equal Opportunity & Privacy

ClickHouse provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type based on factors such as race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

Please see here for our Privacy Statement.

You will launch, run and scale our paid media campaigns, and you will turn user insight into experiments and optimizations that make every visit count.

jobs.title: AI Native Head Of Growth - EdTech (French fluent 🇫🇷)
jobs.description:
This Isn’t Another Growth Job

Most growth teams call themselves data-driven. They have a dashboard, an agency and a ChatGPT licence to write ad copy faster. That’s the 99%.

We want to be part of the 0.1%: a company where AI doesn’t just help the growth team, it runs the growth loop. Every day, on every channel.

Then it’s your chance to define a new category : The Operating System (OS) for Human Greatness Augmented with AI.

Science-backed. Design-led. AI-powered. Global.

We’re not looking for someone who only advises on what to test, we’re looking for someone who builds it. A hands-on Head of Growth who can ideate, write the copy, design the strategy and launch experiments directly.

What Ai-native Growth Means At Paradox 🤖

Our growth machine has to be able to:

• Generate hypotheses. Read the signals (ad performance, webinar attendance, sales calls, objections, churn reasons, comments, competitors’ ads) and propose what to test next, with a cost and an expected impact.

• Act across every tool. Not a chatbot in a tab: it reads and writes in our whole stack, from ad accounts to CRM, landing pages, webinars, email, social DMs and analytics.

• Hold the full context of Paradox. Our DNA, offers, voice, member stories, past campaigns and what they taught us, in one shared company brain.

• Ship its hypotheses. Produce the hook, the ad cut, the page, the email sequence or the funnel variant, and put it live.

• Measure with real KPIs. Every test is tied to a number that matters (cost per qualified lead, show-up rate, close rate, CAC, payback, LTV), not to likes or reach.

• Learn and loop on its own. Scale what works, kill what doesn’t, write the lesson back into the brain, and launch the next cycle without waiting for a meeting.

This is already real. Our growth hub tracks every hypothesis and experiment, with its result. An ads library of thousands of creatives feeds our creative research. Agents cut ads from long-form content, prepare webinars, wire Instagram comment-to-DM automations and audit our tracking after every live. Athena, our AI coach, works with members every day.

OUR MISSION

At Paradox,

We believe self-help is broken: generic theory, a quick high, no real change.

We believe people deserve more. More than content. More than motivation.

They deserve a system that knows them, one that adapts, challenges, and grows with them.

Growth at Paradox means bringing people into something that actually changes their life, and proving it.

We do that by merging :

• Human Intelligence (coaches, peers, and mentors)

• Structured Intelligence (protocols, mental models, rituals)

• Technological Intelligence (AI personalization, feedback loops, adaptive journeys)

To create one seamless ecosystem: Paradox OS.

Short history

Paradox was founded by David Laroche, a creator followed by over 2 million people and known for his interviews with icons like Tony Parker, Mike Horn, Richard Branson and Gad Elmaleh. We started in French. We’re building for the world.

Here’s the bet: a company that learns by itself grows in a way a company of people alone can’t. A small growth team running a self-learning machine can out-test, out-learn and out-grow teams a hundred times its size.

We hold ourselves to the standards of Apple, Spotify and MasterClass. While others hide their numbers, we let our results speak.

YOUR MISSION 🚀

As Head of Growth, you’ll be the architect of a growth machine that learns by itself. In a classic growth team, people do the work and AI helps. Here it’s the other way round: agents do the work, you design the system, set the bar and make the calls.

You don’t just manage a team, you get your hands dirty to identify growth levers and pull them yourself.

🎯 YOUR 5 MAIN MISSIONS

• Build the agents that run growth

• ❌ The old way: a Head of Growth hires people and agencies, briefs them, and checks their work.

• 🏴‍☠️ At Paradox: your team is mostly agents, and you build them yourself. You write their skills, plug them into our tools (ad accounts, CRM, webinars, email, analytics) and write the evals that tell an agent what "good" means: a hook that stops the scroll, a page that converts, a test that’s worth its cost.

• You give autonomy step by step: first an agent suggests, then it acts once you approve, then it acts alone within a budget and guardrails. You move each agent up a level only when its track record earns it.

• Example: in your first month you build the agent that reviews every ad set overnight. At first it only suggests. By month three it pauses losers and moves budget by itself within limits you set, and you only see what was decided and why.

• Build an acquisition engine that runs day and night

• ❌ The old way: a media buyer checks the dashboards each morning, changes bids by hand and waits for the weekly report.

• 🏴‍☠️ At Paradox: you build and improve the agents that watch every ad set, page, webinar and email sequence around the clock. They spot what’s dropping, find the cause, fix it or launch a variant, and report what they did.

• You give autonomy step by step: an agent can pause an ad on its own long before it can raise a budget. You decide where each agent stops and a human takes over.

• Example: show-up rate drops on Tuesday’s webinar. Before anyone notices, an agent has found the cause (a reminder that never went out), fixed it and started testing a new reminder sequence.

• Build a creative machine with taste

• ❌ The old way: a creative team briefs an agency, waits two weeks and gets five ads.

• 🏴‍☠️ At Paradox: you build the agents that turn every live, interview and member story into hooks, ad cuts and shorts, that study what the best advertisers in the world are running, and that write in our voice.

• Your taste becomes the eval: you write down what makes a great hook, a great cut and a great story, in rules and examples the agents check themselves against. Each time you reject something, the reason goes back into the rules.

• Example: one webinar becomes dozens of hook variants by the next morning. You keep the best few, and next week the agents’ first drafts are already closer to your bar.

• Build measurement that checks itself

• ❌ The old way: an analyst rebuilds the numbers in a spreadsheet at the end of the month, and nobody trusts them.

• 🏴‍☠️ At Paradox: you build the agents that connect every touch to cash, from ad to lead, live, sale and transformed member, and that audit the tracking after every campaign.

Stock y surtido

jobs.title: CRO Specialist
jobs.description:
Company Description

Publicis Groupe, the world's second largest communications group, is a solutions platform that is present in more than 100 countries and has more than 98,000 employees. With a unique work philosophy, The Power of One puts clients at the center by promoting the growth of their business through creative agencies (Publicis, Leo Burnett, Publicis Health), media (Zenith, Starcom, Spark and Performics), and areas of transversal knowledge.

Publicis Groupe links Creativity, Technology and Data offering a value proposition that effectively connects brand and consumer.

Overview

We are looking for a CRO Specialist to lead the optimization of the digital experience through experimentation, UX/UI, and user behavior analysis. This person will play a key role in improving website and app conversion rates by combining data-driven insights with design thinking .

Responsibilities

• Design and execute experiments (A/B tests, multivariate testing) focused on data-driven optimization and visual performance.

• Identify friction points throughout the conversion funnel using analytics tools, heatmaps, and qualitative research.

• Propose and prototype design improvements aimed at increasing conversion rates (landing pages, user flows, UI components).

• Collaborate with Product, Marketing, and Development teams to implement and launch experiments.

• Analyze test results and translate findings into actionable insights.

• Maintain and prioritize an experimentation backlog based on business impact.

Ensure visual consistency while optimizing micro-interactions to improve conversion

Qualifications

• 2 years of experience in Conversion Rate Optimization (CRO)

• Hands-on experience with experimentation platforms such as VWO, Optimizely, AB Tasty, or similar tools.

• Strong analytical skills with experience using Google Analytics, Mixpanel, Amplitude, or equivalent analytics platforms.

• An experimentation mindset with a strong results-oriented approach.

Nice to Have

• Basic front-end knowledge (HTML, CSS, JavaScript).

• Experience using Figma to present experiments and design hypotheses.

• Previous experience in e-commerce, SaaS, or growth-focused teams.

• Background in user research or behavioral science.

Employee benefits are an integral part of the company’s annual compensation package. These benefits are subject to the company’s current policies and guidelines and may be modified, updated, or adjusted at the company’s discretion to reflect organizational needs, regulatory requirements, or business conditions.

We are certified as a Great Place to Work , your happiness and providing you with an outstanding experience means a lot to us, let's enjoy!

Here at Publicis Groupe, we are committed to building a culturally diverse workforce and therefore strongly encourage applications from underrepresented groups. We are committed to equality of opportunity and welcome applications from all individuals, regardless of their background: we do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, marital status, or any individual´s status in any group or class protected by law.

jobs.title: CRO Specialist
jobs.description:
About the role We are looking for a curious, thorough and commercially minded CRO Specialist to join our CX & CRO Management team under Ecommerce Operations. Your starting question will be: “What is stopping someone from buying today?” Working with a high degree of autonomy, you will independently identify conversion issues and improvement opportunities across a portfolio of ecommerce retailers, using judgement to determine the appropriate depth of investigation and engaging the teams responsible for delivering changes.
The role combines independent day-to-day monitoring with deep-dive analysis across complex and varied business questions. You will balance timely action on emerging issues with a prioritised programme of short- and medium-term improvements, receiving general direction on new priorities rather than detailed oversight of day-to-day work.
Using GA4, Shopify Analytics, ESW’s internal BI data and behavioural tools, you will explore international shopper behaviour across fashion, luxury, consumer goods and digital goods. You will turn evidence into practical recommendations for Customer Success Managers and retailer partners.
What you’ll doConversion monitoring and ownership
• Independently monitor conversion and funnel progression by retailer, geography, device and traffic source, using consistent metric definitions and meaningful comparisons to identify where attention is required.

• Detect unusual changes, pinpoint the affected funnel stage and independently assess tracking and data quality before investigating shopper behaviour. Exercise judgement to determine the appropriate action within agreed operating practices.

• Own the triage of conversion losses, coordinate cross-functional investigation and track recovery with minimal day-to-day supervision. Maintain accountability for performance follow-up while technical and operational teams own implementation.

Deep-dive analysis and conversion improvements
• Independently combine funnel data, behavioural evidence and commercial context to understand why shoppers abandon their journey, evaluating alternative explanations before reaching a conclusion.

• Analyse complex and varied patterns across markets, brand categories and traffic profiles, accounting for shopper intent, localisation and local expectations.

• Develop evidence-based hypotheses and independently prioritise improvements by conversion impact, commercial value, effort and confidence. Quantify opportunities where the evidence supports it and recommend the appropriate course of action.

• Recommend changes and A/B tests for CX roadmaps, using professional judgement to shape the analysis and test approach. Evaluate outcomes against suitable baselines, accounting for traffic shifts, seasonality and data limitations.

Communication and ways of working
• Proactively share concise performance updates, findings and recommendations with Customer Success Managers and retailer partners, tailoring the level of detail to the audience and confidently explaining the rationale behind recommendations.

• Independently manage priorities across the assigned retailer portfolio, escalating material risks or dependencies when appropriate. Build stakeholder alignment and share reusable learnings that contribute to broader team goals.

• Work autonomously with data and technical teams to resolve access, tracking gaps and reporting needs. Develop AI-assisted workflows to reduce repetitive work, validating outputs before use and sharing effective practices with the wider team.

What we’re looking forMust have
• Fluent English communication. We don't require a certification, but you must be able to lead meetings in English.

• 3+ years of experience in ecommerce analytics, digital analytics, conversion rate optimisation or a similar data-focused role .

• An investigative mindset and the ability to work fully independently, with the rigour to evaluate identifiable factors, test alternative explanations and determine an appropriate course of action.

• Strong hands-on GA4 expertise in ecommerce funnels and segmentation.

• Ability to interpret international shopper behaviour in the context of local markets, brand positioning and acquisition channels.

• Commercial judgement to balance potential value, investigation depth and timely action, making sound decisions with minimal day-to-day instruction.

• Clear writing and presentation skills for both technical and non-technical audiences.

• A collaborative and accountable approach to independently managing work across retailers, following through on agreed actions and providing informal guidance or mentoring to junior colleagues when appropriate.

Nice to have
• Working knowledge of Shopify Analytics, BI platforms and behavioural analytics tools. Able to apply professional knowledge creatively to solve unfamiliar problems.

• Strong Excel or Google Sheets and reporting skills, with experience in AI-assisted analysis or automation.

• Sound understanding of data quality, experiment evaluation and attribution limits.

About ESW Our purpose is simple: to create moments that matter between people and the brands they cherish. We enable brands to expand their global reach, facilitating simple and seamless ecommerce experiences for consumers worldwide. Through our integration solutions, we deliver a complete international checkout experience, including local duties, taxes, fulfilment, delivery management, and global returns and payment processing capabilities.
Guided by our values—Own It, Champion Simplicity, Win as One, and Debate then Commit—we strive to foster innovation, accountability, and teamwork, creating solutions that inspire trust and drive impactful results.
What's on offer?
• Direct hire with a product company: This isn’t consulting or outsourcing. Shape the future of our product with ownership, impact, and long-term vision.

jobs.title: AI Native Head Of Growth - EdTech (French fluent 🇫🇷)
jobs.description:
This Isn’t Another Growth Job

Most growth teams call themselves data-driven. They have a dashboard, an agency and a ChatGPT licence to write ad copy faster. That’s the 99%.

We want to be part of the 0.1%: a company where AI doesn’t just help the growth team, it runs the growth loop. Every day, on every channel.

Then it’s your chance to define a new category : The Operating System (OS) for Human Greatness Augmented with AI.

Science-backed. Design-led. AI-powered. Global.

We’re not looking for someone who only advises on what to test, we’re looking for someone who builds it. A hands-on Head of Growth who can ideate, write the copy, design the strategy and launch experiments directly.

What Ai-native Growth Means At Paradox 🤖

Our growth machine has to be able to:

• Generate hypotheses. Read the signals (ad performance, webinar attendance, sales calls, objections, churn reasons, comments, competitors’ ads) and propose what to test next, with a cost and an expected impact.

• Act across every tool. Not a chatbot in a tab: it reads and writes in our whole stack, from ad accounts to CRM, landing pages, webinars, email, social DMs and analytics.

• Hold the full context of Paradox. Our DNA, offers, voice, member stories, past campaigns and what they taught us, in one shared company brain.

• Ship its hypotheses. Produce the hook, the ad cut, the page, the email sequence or the funnel variant, and put it live.

• Measure with real KPIs. Every test is tied to a number that matters (cost per qualified lead, show-up rate, close rate, CAC, payback, LTV), not to likes or reach.

• Learn and loop on its own. Scale what works, kill what doesn’t, write the lesson back into the brain, and launch the next cycle without waiting for a meeting.

This is already real. Our growth hub tracks every hypothesis and experiment, with its result. An ads library of thousands of creatives feeds our creative research. Agents cut ads from long-form content, prepare webinars, wire Instagram comment-to-DM automations and audit our tracking after every live. Athena, our AI coach, works with members every day.

OUR MISSION

At Paradox,

We believe self-help is broken: generic theory, a quick high, no real change.

We believe people deserve more. More than content. More than motivation.

They deserve a system that knows them, one that adapts, challenges, and grows with them.

Growth at Paradox means bringing people into something that actually changes their life, and proving it.

We do that by merging :

• Human Intelligence (coaches, peers, and mentors)

• Structured Intelligence (protocols, mental models, rituals)

• Technological Intelligence (AI personalization, feedback loops, adaptive journeys)

To create one seamless ecosystem: Paradox OS.

Short history

Paradox was founded by David Laroche, a creator followed by over 2 million people and known for his interviews with icons like Tony Parker, Mike Horn, Richard Branson and Gad Elmaleh. We started in French. We’re building for the world.

Here’s the bet: a company that learns by itself grows in a way a company of people alone can’t. A small growth team running a self-learning machine can out-test, out-learn and out-grow teams a hundred times its size.

We hold ourselves to the standards of Apple, Spotify and MasterClass. While others hide their numbers, we let our results speak.

YOUR MISSION 🚀

As Head of Growth, you’ll be the architect of a growth machine that learns by itself. In a classic growth team, people do the work and AI helps. Here it’s the other way round: agents do the work, you design the system, set the bar and make the calls.

You don’t just manage a team, you get your hands dirty to identify growth levers and pull them yourself.

🎯 YOUR 5 MAIN MISSIONS

• Build the agents that run growth

• ❌ The old way: a Head of Growth hires people and agencies, briefs them, and checks their work.

• 🏴‍☠️ At Paradox: your team is mostly agents, and you build them yourself. You write their skills, plug them into our tools (ad accounts, CRM, webinars, email, analytics) and write the evals that tell an agent what "good" means: a hook that stops the scroll, a page that converts, a test that’s worth its cost.

• You give autonomy step by step: first an agent suggests, then it acts once you approve, then it acts alone within a budget and guardrails. You move each agent up a level only when its track record earns it.

• Example: in your first month you build the agent that reviews every ad set overnight. At first it only suggests. By month three it pauses losers and moves budget by itself within limits you set, and you only see what was decided and why.

• Build an acquisition engine that runs day and night

• ❌ The old way: a media buyer checks the dashboards each morning, changes bids by hand and waits for the weekly report.

• 🏴‍☠️ At Paradox: you build and improve the agents that watch every ad set, page, webinar and email sequence around the clock. They spot what’s dropping, find the cause, fix it or launch a variant, and report what they did.

• You give autonomy step by step: an agent can pause an ad on its own long before it can raise a budget. You decide where each agent stops and a human takes over.

• Example: show-up rate drops on Tuesday’s webinar. Before anyone notices, an agent has found the cause (a reminder that never went out), fixed it and started testing a new reminder sequence.

• Build a creative machine with taste

• ❌ The old way: a creative team briefs an agency, waits two weeks and gets five ads.

• 🏴‍☠️ At Paradox: you build the agents that turn every live, interview and member story into hooks, ad cuts and shorts, that study what the best advertisers in the world are running, and that write in our voice.

• Your taste becomes the eval: you write down what makes a great hook, a great cut and a great story, in rules and examples the agents check themselves against. Each time you reject something, the reason goes back into the rules.

• Example: one webinar becomes dozens of hook variants by the next morning. You keep the best few, and next week the agents’ first drafts are already closer to your bar.

• Build measurement that checks itself

• ❌ The old way: an analyst rebuilds the numbers in a spreadsheet at the end of the month, and nobody trusts them.

• 🏴‍☠️ At Paradox: you build the agents that connect every touch to cash, from ad to lead, live, sale and transformed member, and that audit the tracking after every campaign.

• No number, no test: you define the KPIs that matter (CAC, show-up, close rate, LTV, payback), and agents refuse to launch a test that isn’t wired to one.

• Example: after each live, an agent cross-checks the ad platform, the CRM and our analytics, finds where they disagree and fixes the leak before the next live.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager

Amenitiz is the all-in-one software behind 15,000 independent hotels in Spain, Portugal, France and Italy. In 2026 we shipped more than ever: POS, Ami and Conversations, fiscal compliance in five countries, and integrations with OTAs, revenue management systems and POS providers.

Our product surface grew faster than three PMs can carry. You'll be the fourth, and you'll own a part of it end to end: from the opportunity, to the code, to hotels using it and paying for it.




HOW PMS WORK HERE

Our PMs open the repo. They prototype with Claude Code in days, ship fixes and small changes themselves, and bring engineers the hard problems with a working prototype in hand.

They spend hours every week with hoteliers: on calls, on visits, in the Care queue. They read their own data in SQL and Mixpanel. And a release is only the start: a feature is done when hotels use it and we can see it in the numbers.




WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - The adoption number for everything you ship

 - A set of hotels you know by name, and the partnerships your initiatives need

 - Launch enablement for Care, Onboarding, Account Management, Sales and Marketing

 - 


YOUR FIRST YEAR

 - Month 3: your own changes in production, and a prototype in front of real hotels

 - Month 6: your first major release live, with an activation target set before launch and tracked from day one

 - Month 12: an initiative that measurably moved revenue for a set of hotels, and the next 6-month roadmap for your area, written by you


YOU HAVE

 - 5+ years as a PM in B2B SaaS, including an initiative you built from scratch and the adoption or retention number it moved

 - Software you built and shipped yourself: prototypes with Claude Code or similar, and fixes merged to production. You can show us something real users used

 - Real time with customers, especially small-business owners, and the instinct to bring back what they'd pay for

 - Experience defining activation, reading the funnel yourself and fixing drop-off in the product

 - Full professional English

 - A base in Barcelona, or the will to move here: we work office-first from Plaça de Catalunya
   
   


BONUS POINTS

 - A background in hospitality, travel, payments or compliance

 - Spanish, French, Italian or Portuguese

 - LLM or agent features in production

 - Experience running a big product surface with a small team
   
   


WHY JOIN

 - Own a chapter of an 18-month plan, at 15,000 hotels in four countries

 - Build with AI the way most PMs only read about

 - Join a team of four PMs where every one of them ships

 - Work with a direct line to our CPO and CEO

 - Live and work in Barcelona

 


OUR OFFER

 - Competitive salary + stock options with a back-loaded vesting schedule

 - Comprehensive health insurance

 - On-demand salary access, no need to wait until the end of the month

 - A structured career path with defined criteria at every level

 - Flexible benefits: save on meals, childcare, transportation and training with tailored remuneration options

 - Any book, purchased for you, plus access to a shared team library

 - An international team of 35+ nationalities based in one of Europe's leading tech hubs




OUR PROCESS

 1. A 30-minute call with Talent Acquisition

 2. A 60-minute call with Marco Riedl, our CPO

jobs.title: Lead Product Manager, DeFi
jobs.description:
Who we are

We simplify wealth creation. Founded in 2014 in Vienna, Austria by Eric Demuth, Paul Klanschek and Christian Trummer, we’re here to help people trust themselves enough to build their financial freedom — for now and the future. Our user-friendly, trade-everything platform empowers both first-time investors and seasoned experts to invest in the cryptocurrencies, crypto indices, stocks*, precious metals and commodities* they want — with any sized budget, 24/7. Our global team works across different cultures and time zones, bringing our products to more than 7 million customers, making us one of Europe’s safest and most secure platforms that powers modern investing.

Headquartered in Austria but operating across Europe, our products are built by fast-moving, talented, “roll-up-your-sleeves-and-make-it-happen” kind of people. It’s these diverse perspectives and innovative minds operating as ONE TEAM that keep Bitpanda at the cutting edge of our industry. So if you’re someone who thinks big, moves fast and wants to make an impact right from day one, then get ready to join our industry-changing team. Let’s go!

Your mission

Bitpanda serves millions of investors across Europe, and we're bringing regulated finance onchain with Vision Chain, our own OP Stack L2 blockchain. We are looking for a Lead Product Manager, DeFi to build Bitpanda’s DeFi ecosystem from the ground up, creating the world’s premier Euro-denominated DeFi ecosystem while making it safe, accessible, and intuitive for our customers.

The first use case is crypto-backed borrowing and lending in the Bitpanda app, with an eye to then build more sophisticated products and use cases leveraging tokenized commodities, securities, funds, and structured products. You’ll decide which protocols and partners come to Vision Chain, and work collaboratively to bring DeFi to Bitpanda customers in a way that feels as simple as the app they already trust. You'll work in a small, senior team with our smart contract engineers and Bitpanda's Legal, Compliance and Risk teams, as an individual contributor reporting to the Head of Web3 Product.

What you’ll do

• Design and run the lending markets: set loan-to-value and liquidation thresholds, interest rate curves, caps, and oracles, while also owning monitoring and incident playbooks.

• Bring liquidity and users to permissioned markets and assets: set supply targets, bring in euro liquidity from stablecoin issuers, institutional lenders, curated vaults and market makers, and work out how verified customers reach these markets, without paying for volume.

• Make sure the right DeFi infrastructure is in place, particularly for permissioned tokenized assets: DEX liquidity deep enough for swaps and liquidations, liquidators, oracles and the other building blocks the markets depend on.

• Shape what customers see, sign, and own in the Bitpanda app, including how liquidation and risk are explained, and measure real use: borrowers who come back, bad debt and revenue, not total value locked alone.

jobs.title: Senior Clinical Product Lead | 100% Remote within Europe
jobs.description:
ABOUT DOCPLANNER AND NOA

Docplanner is a global healthcare platform connecting more than 300,000 doctors with approximately 100 million patients every month across 13 markets.

Within Docplanner, Noa is on a mission to help people live longer, healthier lives. We build AI that works alongside doctors to:

 - Remove their administrative work.

 - Help them make better decisions and handle repeatable cases, so they can spend their time where it matters most.

 - Help patients navigate healthcare using their medical history as personalized context.

We're already in doctors' hands: Noa Notes takes documentation off their plates, while Noa Evidence brings trustworthy medical evidence to the point of care.

The next frontier is the hardest—and the most valuable: helping doctors, and eventually patients, make decisions while our AI safely takes on repeatable clinical work. That's where a doctor's judgment has to live inside the product itself. That's this role.




ABOUT THE ROLE

You’ll help take Noa from writing notes and providing evidence to helping doctors decide—ensuring what we build fits clinical workflows and earns doctors’ trust.

This isn’t a traditional CMO, advisory or regulatory role. It is a hands-on, individual-contributor clinical-product role. You will:

 - Shape doctor-facing products by bringing real clinical needs and workflows into product decisions.

 - Bring clinical judgment to what we build, including what is correct, useful and safe.

Because you’re a doctor yourself, you can talk to our users peer-to-peer and get the honest answers a survey never will. As our first dedicated clinical hire on the product, you’ll help establish how clinical expertise informs Docplanner’s AI products.

You’ll work day-to-day with Product, AI, Design, Engineering, Regulatory and our doctor network.




WHAT YOU’LL DO


SHAPE WHAT WE BUILD

 - Bring how doctors really work—their habits, workflows and administrative realities—into the product.

 - Talk to doctors across specialties and working styles, and turn candid feedback into product decisions.

 - Partner with Product, Design and Engineering to prioritise and ship improvements, then learn from how doctors use them.


BRING CLINICAL JUDGMENT INTO THE PRODUCT

 - Help define what correct, useful and safe looks like for our doctor-facing AI products.

 - Review prompts, outputs, clinical templates and workflows, and identify clinically meaningful failure modes.

 - Turn clinician feedback and evaluation findings into product and model improvements with Product, ML/LLM and evaluation partners.


KEEP IT SAFE AND SCALABLE

 - Work with Product, ML/LLM, Regulatory and the PRRC to align product intent, evidence, risks and controls.

 - Build practical feedback loops with practising clinicians and our consultant-doctor network.


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - A medical degree and at least 2 years of direct clinical practice. Active licensure and current practice are not required.

 - Meaningful experience shaping and shipping a doctor-facing or clinical product, either as a clinical product leader or a clinician-founder/builder.

 - You personally owned product decisions, worked directly with Product, Design and Engineering, and shipped something clinicians used.

 - You’ve turned clinical problems into product decisions—not just provided advice, review or governance.

 - You combine strong clinical judgment with doctor discovery, workflow understanding and a focus on trust and adoption.

 - You communicate clearly and directly across clinical, product, technical, regulatory and leadership teams.

 - You’re comfortable operating independently as a senior, hands-on contributor in a lean cross-functional team.

 - You actively use generative AI and understand its potential and limitations. Hands-on experience with prompting, output review or AI-assisted development tools is valuable.

Bonus: Experience with ambient documentation, clinical templates, medical-knowledge systems, clinical coding or regulated Software as a Medical Device.




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE AFTER 6 MONTHS

 - A clear, evidence-backed view of the priority doctor workflows and product opportunities Noa should address.

 - Product improvements shipped based on doctor discovery, feedback and observed usage.

 - Clear clinical quality expectations and feedback loops established with Product, ML/LLM and evaluation partners.


WHY JOIN NOA AT DOCPLANNER

 - Real impact at real scale: Your work reaches hundreds of thousands of doctors and their patients.

 - Shape what comes next: You’ll influence what Noa and Docplanner’s AI products become—and whether doctors and patients trust them.

 - Ship to learn: A feature in front of users beats another month of planning.

 - Work flexibly: The role is 100% remote across eligible European locations, subject to local hiring arrangements.

jobs.title: Senior FX Product Manager - Hedging Conversion
jobs.description:
Ebury helps ambitious businesses unlock global growth, and we take the same approach with our people. We encourage innovation and movement, collaboration and problem-solving, and foster an environment where everyone can feel they belong, are valued, supported and empowered to succeed.

If you’re a collaborator who wants to help transform how businesses operate globally, get in touch - we’d love to discuss how Ebury can accelerate your career so you can shape the future.

FX Senior Product Manager - Hedging conversion

Ebury Madrid Office - Hybrid: 4 days in the office, 1 day working from home per week

As Ebury scales globally, we are evolving from a delivery-led organisation into a platform-led product company - building shared foundations that allow teams to move faster, operate safely in regulated environments and deliver high-quality client experiences across channel

The Opportunity

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to own one number: the share of Ebury's clients who convert into hedgers — and to build the journeys, workflows and decision tools that get them there.

Ebury has a real hedging business. Thousands of clients already hedge with us, they're our most valuable and stickiest, and Hedge works. The problem isn't proof of concept — it's rate. For every client who converts, several more carry the same currency exposure, would benefit from the same forward, and never get there.

Here's the honest reason why. Hedging isn't a product you sell; it's a conclusion a client reaches once they can see what their international business is actually exposed to. Today that seeing happens in a CPM's head and a spreadsheet, one client at a time. The client can't see their own exposure clearly, the CPM can't see it at scale, and so the conversation that should be obvious either happens late or never happens at all.

This role builds the layer that changes that: guided journeys and lifecycle workflows that carry a client from unaware exposure to a first hedge to a standing policy — and the decision tools that let both the client and their CPM understand the client's international business well enough to make the right call, not just the next call.

You'll sit at the intersection of product, data, and commercial, working closely with:

• CPMs and Sales teams who convert clients today

• Data and Analytics

• Design and Engineering

• Compliance and Risk

• Clients directly

What you’ll do

You will own the end-to-end conversion journey into hedging, backed by a dedicated squad of developers, including:

Journeys & Lifecycle Workflows

• The path from spot client → Hedge-active → policy client, and every drop-off point along it

• Guided, staged journeys rather than one-off prompts: the right message, to the right client, at the moment their exposure is real to them

• Triggered workflows off real events, a new currency pair, a large invoice, a rate move against them, a forward maturing

• Understanding what separates the clients who convert from the ones who don't, and building for the difference

Decision Tools for Clients

• Showing a client what their international business is actually exposed to, in their own numbers and their own currencies

• Exposure views, scenario and impact modelling, MTM and forward comparisons a finance lead can act on without training

• Turning "should I hedge?" into a question the client can answer for themselves, with confidence

• Balancing honesty about risk against simplicity of decision, the goal is a well-made decision, not a sold one

Tooling for CPMs

• Giving CPMs a portfolio-level view of client exposure, trades and performance, so they know who to talk to and what to say before the client asks

• Surfacing the signals that make a conversation timely: unhedged exposure, changing trade patterns, policy lapses

• Learning from the conversations that already convert clients, and productising them

Repeat Hedging & Policy

• Turning a first hedge into a second and a third

• Moving clients from ad-hoc trades onto a standing hedging policy they run every month

• Statements, notifications and review moments that build the habit and prove the value after the fact

Experimentation & Measurement

• A cadence of A/B tests across the journey, not a feature backlog

• Reading results honestly, including the ones that kill your own ideas

• Building the measurement so conversion, and what's driving it

What success looks like (12-18 months)

• Spot-to-hedger conversion rate is measurably higher, and you can attribute the lift

• A meaningful share of new hedgers convert through product journeys rather than a CPM conversation

• CPMs work from exposure signals in a tool instead of instinct and spreadsheets, and cover more clients as a result

• Clients can articulate their own FX exposure — and clients who hedge once come back without being called

• More hedgers move onto hedging policies rather than trading ad hoc

• Product — not people — becomes the primary driver of hedging conversion

What makes this role hard

• You're changing behaviour, not shipping features. The instrument already exists and works; the reason more clients don't use it is understanding, trust and habit.

• It's a two-sided problem. Clients and CPMs need different views of the same truth, and building for one badly makes the other worse but the CPMs must know what the client can see to have consultative conversations

• The baseline isn't zero. There's an existing business and an existing way of converting clients, you have to improve on it without disrupting it.

• Exposure is genuinely hard to model. Client data is incomplete, trade history is a proxy for intent, and being confidently wrong about someone's exposure destroys trust instantly.

• You're helping non-experts make decisions with real financial consequences. Oversimplify and you mislead; don't simplify and nobody acts.

• You'll navigate real-world complexity: regional and regulatory nuance, credit and margin implications, and client segments with genuinely different needs.

Who we are looking for

Prior FX or hedging experience is a plus, not a requirement. We're looking for someone who can move a hard conversion number in a complex, regulated environment — with strong agency, sharp analytical instincts, and a real feel for why people do and don't act.

Must-have:

• 4+ years of product management experience, including at least one role owning conversion, adoption or engagement outcomes end-to-end

• Strong analytics and experimentation skills — funnel analysis, cohort and retention analysis, designing and interpreting A/B tests

• Experience designing lifecycle journeys or triggered workflows, and the messaging that carries them

• Fluent English (daily collaboration with global commercial, tech and Legal/Compliance/Risk stakeholders)

Nice-to-have:

• Familiarity with foreign exchange, hedging or other asset classes

• Experience in fintech or regulated financial products

jobs.title: Director of Product Management, Observability
jobs.description:
Elastic, the Search AI Company, enables everyone to find the answers they need in real time, using all their data, at scale — unleashing the potential of businesses and people. The Elastic Search AI Platform, used by more than 50% of the Fortune 500, brings together the precision of search and the intelligence of AI to enable everyone to accelerate the results that matter. By taking advantage of all structured and unstructured data — securing and protecting private information more effectively — Elastic’s complete, cloud-based solutions for search, security, and observability help organizations deliver on the promise of AI.

What is The Role

Every outcome on the Elastic platform starts with data getting in. Streams, Elastic’s telemetry pipeline, is the shared ingest layer for Observability, Security, and Search. It collects data from any source, processes and routes it, and stores it in Elasticsearch or the customer’s own object storage, all built on open standards like OpenTelemetry and Prometheus. As Director of Product Management, you will own Streams end to end and lead the PM team behind it. Your job is to make Elastic the easiest platform to bring data to, for every solution and every customer.

Location: Madrid - we will only consider candidates already based in Madrid or open to relocation.

Fever is growing through acquisition as well as organically - we expect to bring more companies into the Fever family over the next few years. Each one arrives with its own product, its own codebase, and its own way of doing things. This role exists to make sure that growth actually compounds instead of creating fragmentation: someone who can walk into an acquired company's stack, understand what's genuinely differentiated versus redundant, and drive the decisions that turn "two products" into "one better product."

Fever already operates at global scale, and acquisitions are how we grow even faster. Every company that joins makes the whole group stronger: together, we’re far more than the sum of our parts.

Every company that joins brings talented teams, strong products and deep expertise in its market. The opportunity is to connect them on one Fever platform, so that what one company builds can power all the others, and every new company gets the scale of Fever from its first day with us.

That’s what this role is about. You’ll shape how the Fever group scales as a platform: the vision and architecture for the capabilities our companies share, the playbook that helps every new company get up and running with Fever, and the hands-on work of making each integration a success. You’ll work across products, markets and teams spanning the whole group, close to the leadership decisions that shape where Fever goes next.

It’s a senior individual contributor role.

About the role

• Define the product vision and strategy for the Fever group platform: decide which capabilities (payments, invoicing, seating maps, access control, box office, point of sale and more) should become shared group services, and work with engineering to productize them so any group company can integrate.

• Own the integration playbook: the standard, prioritized path every acquired company follows to run on Fever’s shared services.

• Assess each acquisition feature by feature, produce a keep / kill / merge plan, and shape integration decisions with engineering leads on APIs, data models and migration.

• Run partner and customer migrations end to end, coordinating BD, account management, operations and support.

• Be the bridge between acquired teams and Fever’s product and engineering org in the first 6–12 months, and report integration progress to leadership.

About you

Basic skills and qualifications

• Degree in Engineering, Computer Science or similar, 5+ years in product management (ideally platform or technical products), and professional English.

• Deep technical fluency: comfortable with architecture, APIs and data models, and with trade-offs like consolidation, migration and build vs. reuse.

• Proven experience building a shared-services strategy and leading post-M&A or platform integration, including keep / kill / merge calls.

• Strong program management in ambiguous, cross-team settings with legacy systems.

• Clear communicator and analytical thinker, with high ownership and urgency.

Preferred skills and qualifications

•

• PM experience in a company that grew through acquisitions, ideally including M&A due diligence.

• Domain knowledge in ticketing, live entertainment or commerce (payments, access control, box office, seating).

• Prior hands-on experience as a backend or platform engineer.

• Track record of earning trust with acquired teams and managing change.

• Experience defining integration metrics and mentoring other PMs.

Benefits & Perks

jobs.title: Product Director
jobs.description:
As Product Director for the Use Case Tribe, you will lead with a clear and ambitious vision for the product organization that turns EcoVadis's strengths into new, market-leading products. The tribe owns our strategic use cases: regulatory due diligence, human rights due diligence, decarbonization, supply chain resilience and sustainable procurement. You will lead and empower a team of Product Managers and Experts, own the tribe's contribution to ARR, and be accountable for launching innovative products that customers buy, adopt and renew.
This is a dual leadership and execution role, not a management-only role. You will set the direction and build the team, and stay hands-on where it matters. We're looking for a high-agency leader who builds before they debate, uses AI to move at a different speed, and takes full ownership of outcomes while creating the space for their people to do the same.
The Use Case Tribe is also expected to be a model for the wider Product organization in how we choose what to build, communicate and work.
Our leadership philosophy
Our leaders are here to guide with a clear and ambitious vision while empowering teams through coaching. You'll play a key role in creating a culture where people are trusted to take accountability, own their growth, and drive impact, all while adapting your approach to meet the moment.
What you'll be doing

• Decide what is worth building and where to invest: Identify the right customer problems and market opportunities, challenge existing assumptions, and turn them into compelling product propositions.

• Allocate focus and investment: Prioritize across use cases, deciding where to invest, where to wait and where to stop, and make trade-offs on scope, sequencing and resourcing with engineering, design and commercial leaders.

• Set and champion the vision and roadmap: Define the end-to-end product strategy and roadmap for our strategic use cases, and the path from parity to market leadership. Align stakeholders around it, communicating with clarity to all audiences.

• Own the commercial outcome: Be accountable for the tribe's ARR contribution together with frontline leaders. Set targets with the leadership team and track performance through leading and lagging indicators.

• Roll up your sleeves: Step in where the work needs you. That may mean unblocking a squad, sharpening a requirement, building a prototype, rewriting a business case, joining a critical customer or partner conversation, or taking on a use case directly when needed.

• Influence architecture across tribes: Work closely with engineering and product leaders in other tribes on shared platforms, data and integration choices. Make the case for the architectural direction our use cases need, and resolve cross-tribe dependencies.

• Drive launches and go-to-market: Partner with sales, marketing, customer success and partnerships to define positioning, pricing and packaging, enablement and launch plans, and to convert products into pipeline and revenue.

• Stay close to customers and the market: Spend real time with buyers, program owners and co-development accounts. Understand how competitors, regulators and partners are shaping the market, and bring that insight into decisions.

• Lead and grow the team: Hire, onboard and develop Product Managers and Experts through coaching and constructive feedback, so they own outcomes end to end.

• Raise AI and product maturity across EcoVadis: Pioneer new AI-first ways of working in the tribe and share them with other Product teams. Contribute to shared standards, practices and coaching that lift the overall capability of Product Management.

Who you are

• A builder and a leader: you are equally comfortable setting strategy and building a rough prototype that teaches the team something.

• Commercially minded: you connect product decisions to revenue, adoption and retention.

• Strong product sense: you have the judgment to know what's worth building and why.

• An AI-native operator: AI is part of how you work, and you're raising the AI fluency of the people around you.

• Customer-obsessed: you get your conviction from talking to real customers and industry stakeholders, testing assumptions and keeping an open mind.

• A multiplier: you make other people better, hire well and develop talent.

• Biased to speed: you move decisively with incomplete information, know which decisions are reversible, remain open to new information and update fast when you're wrong.

• A strong influencer without needing full control: you see building relationships across tribes as part of the craft.

• An exceptional communicator: you simplify complexity, tell a compelling story, and earn trust with people at all levels, including executives.

AI fluency we hire for
We expect you to operate at the AI-Fluent to AI-Native end of the spectrum. You don't just use AI for one-off tasks. You rebuild core product workflows around it: agents configured with product context, personas and prior research; machine-testable acceptance criteria; reusable workflows shared with the team. As a leader, you will help shift the team from feature author to outcome orchestrator, concentrating on strategic trade-offs and novel bets while agents carry more of the discovery and synthesis.

• Typically 10+ years of product management experience, including 3+ years leading Product Managers, with a track record of owning a significant B2B enterprise SaaS portfolio and its commercial results (ARR, revenue growth, adoption or retention).

• Experience launching new products from zero to one and scaling them, with real business and customer outcomes to point to.

• A proven ability to set a product strategy and roadmap, and to bring executives, engineers, sales and customers along with it.

• Strong technical fluency: you can discuss architecture, data and integration trade-offs credibly with engineering leaders, and prototype with AI tooling, LLM APIs and a scripting language (Python / JavaScript or equivalent) where it helps.

• Experience influencing across teams without direct authority, including shared platforms and data.

• Experience working with commercial teams on pricing, packaging and go-to-market.

• Comfort operating in a regulated, data-rich, sustainability or risk domain, or the curiosity and speed to get there fast.

• Fluent English (our primary working language).

In return for your expertise, we offer:

• Support with all the necessary office and IT equipment

As a Senior Product Manager for one of our Strategic Use Cases, you will own that use case end-to-end — from the customer problem and the data it depends on, through prototype, roadmap and launch, to the outcome in the market. You will work alongside senior engineers and product experts to define the ambition, understand requirements and launch innovative new products.
This is a builder role, not a coordination role. We're looking for a high-agency generalist who prototypes before they debate, uses AI to move at a different speed, engages customers directly, and takes full ownership of outcomes — not output.
What you'll be doing

• Own the vision: Set and drive the aligned, end-to-end vision for your use case (regulatory due diligence, human rights due diligence, decarbonization or resilience)— what the customer experience should be, where the gaps are, and the sequence from parity to leadership.

• Understand the market: Understand the technical requirements of your use case, and how other competitors and customers are currently solving it. Take inspiration from everywhere, including partner discussions, conferences, webinars and other resources.

• Engage customers directly: Spend real time with buyers, program owners and co-development accounts. Validate problems and solutions first-hand; and build interest from customers and prospects.

• Prototype with AI: Use AI prototyping tools to build working demos, spin up lightweight services and test your own assumptions before committing engineering. Show the team what's possible by doing it, not describing it.

• Drive the build forward: Work alongside engineering to unblock and drive the build forward, working across multiple areas of the product and platform, collaborating with other tribes and squads whilst executing independently or in partnership.

• Partner on go-to-market: Work hand-in-hand with the Strategic Use Case Leads and commercial teams to land what you build.

• Own the outcome: Define the measures of success, hold yourself and the circle to them, and lead clean persist / pivot / stop decisions.

Who you are

• A generalist builder at heart — you move fluidly between strategy, data, prototype and GTM, and you'd rather build a rough thing that teaches you something than debate a perfect thing that doesn't.

• An AI-native operator — AI is woven through how you work: discovery, analysis, prototyping, instrumentation and communication.

• Customer-obsessed — you get your conviction from talking to real customers, not from the building.

• Biased to speed — you move decisively with incomplete information, tell reversible decisions from irreversible ones, and update fast when you're wrong. Strong opinions, loosely held.

• Comfortable without full control — part of your use case's scope and experience will always be owned by other squads. You see managing that, as the craft.

• Mission-driven — you want your work to help guide all companies toward a sustainable world, and to help EcoVadis lead the market in getting there.

AI fluency we hire for
We expect you to operate at the AI-Fluent to AI-Native end of the spectrum: you don't just use AI for one-off tasks, you reconstruct core PM workflows around it — agents configured with your product context, personas and prior research; machine-testable acceptance criteria; reusable workflows you share with the squad. At the top of this ladder, the PM shifts from feature author to outcome orchestrator — concentrating on strategic trade-offs and novel bets while agents carry more of the discovery and synthesis.

• Typically 10+ years experience, including a track record owning a meaningful product area end-to-end in B2B enterprise SaaS, with real business and customer outcomes to point to.

• Enough technical fluency to build — you can prototype with AI tooling, LLM APIs and a scripting language (Python / JavaScript or equivalent) without waiting for engineering to validate every idea.

• An AI-native way of working that's already part of how you operate, not an aspiration.

• Comfort operating in a regulated, data-rich, sustainability or risk domain — or the curiosity and speed to get there fast.

• Sharp problem framing and communication — you walk into the room with a recommendation, not an open question, and you make engineering and design faster by reducing ambiguity.

• Be fluent in English (as our primary working language).

jobs.title: Lead Product Manager - Advertising
jobs.description:
WELCOME TO OLX
 
We're building marketplace sustainable ecosystems that millions of people depend on every month – to buy and sell cars, find homes, land jobs, and trade secondhand goods. It's commerce that matters: safe, smart, and environmentally responsible.
 
We do this with courage to innovate, commitment to outcomes, collaboration across 50+ nationalities and 7 markets, and a customer-led approach that puts real people first. Add a desire to win – and you get a culture that's ambitious, fast-moving, and built on trust.
 
Our brands – including AutoTrader, OLX, Otomoto Property24, and more – are loved by millions. And we're backed by Prosus, one of the world's largest tech investors.
 
Join OLX and see how far you can go.


About the role
 
Advertising is one of OLX's most important revenue lines - and one of its biggest opportunities. Today, our advertising business spans multiple markets, formats, and platforms, but it needs a product leader who can take it to the next level: from foundational ad-tech infrastructure to new revenue surfaces powered by AI.
 
We are looking for a Lead Product Manager to own the global advertising product end-to-end. This means everything from the ad-core stack (serving, auction, targeting, measurement) to growing revenue beyond listings through self-serve advertiser tools, programmatic demand, and retail-media formats. You'll also shape how advertising integrates into AI-native surfaces — balancing monetisation yield against buyer experience.
 
This is a role for someone who has built advertising products at scale, understands the programmatic ecosystem, and is excited about using AI to create new advertising experiences. You'll work closely with business and commercial stakeholders to grow revenue, while ensuring our advertising never compromises the trust our users place in the platform.
 
This role reports to the Head of Product.
What you'll do
Own the global advertising product end-to-end: ad-core stack (serving, auction, targeting, measurement) across all marketplaces and platforms
Drive growth of advertising revenue beyond listings, including self-serve advertiser tools, programmatic demand, and retail-media formats such as sponsored listings, native, and video
Own integration of ads into AI-native surfaces such as AutoIQ and agentic search, balancing yield against buyer experience
Define and track advertising success metrics: revenue, fill rate, eCPM, advertiser ROI, buyer experience impact
Partner closely with Engineering, Data Science, Commercial, and Sales teams to build the product capabilities that unlock revenue growth
Represent the advertising product at the leadership level, presenting strategy and results to executive audiences
What we're looking for
Significant product management experience in digital advertising, ad-tech, monetisation, or revenue product at scale
Proven track record of building and scaling advertising products — programmatic ads, third-party ads, billing systems, or ad-serving platforms
Experience taking advertising or monetisation products from early-stage to meaningful revenue
Ability to balance monetisation yield with user experience — making evidence-based trade-offs between revenue and buyer trust
AI-native: you build with AI, not just use it for productivity. You experiment with AI tools outside of work and bring that curiosity into your product craft
Zero-to-one: you see opportunities, not just optimisations. You spot problems, build prototypes, and ship
Comfortable with ambiguity: you don't wait for perfect clarity — you create it
Strong stakeholder management across commercial, engineering, and executive audiences
 
Preferred:
 
Experience with retail media, sponsored listings, native advertising, or video ad formats in a marketplace or e-commerce context
Familiarity with AI-native product surfaces and how advertising integrates with AI experiences
Multi-market experience across different regulatory and commercial environments


Diversity, Equity and Inclusion at OLX
OLX values diversity and welcomes applicants of all races, ethnicities, disabilities, ages, genders, sexual orientations, religions, backgrounds, and experiences to apply. If this role excites you, we encourage you to apply, even if you don’t meet all the requirements - you may be just the right fit for this or other opportunities with us!
 
OLX will process your personal data to assess your fit for the applied position. You may optionally consent to store your data for up to 12 months after the application process for consideration in future OLX roles. For more details on how your application data will be processed please check our Privacy Statement.
